merge_blocked_reason: push to main triggers build-image.yml, which publishes a multi-arch image to GHCR tagged :0.44.0 and :latest

findings.title: Unused nodemailer ships in the production image with 8 HIGH advisories
findings.summary: nodemailer was a production dependency of the server workspace and therefore installed into the runtime image by `npm ci --omit=dev`, while never being imported anywhere (email goes through the platform's /api/fabric/email). It carried eight HIGH advisories including SMTP command injection, CRLF header injection, TLS certificate validation bypass, and file read / SSRF via the message-level raw option. @react-pdf/renderer and react were dead the same way after the v0.35.0 descope. Not reachable, but a mail library with SMTP-injection flaws has no business inside a payments container, and it accounted for 7 of 15 audit findings.

findings.title: reallocateStudent scans the entire payment_allocations table on every money write
findings.summary: The allocation-clearing read selected every row of payment_allocations for every student and discarded non-matching rows in JavaScript, so the cost of one payment was proportional to every allocation the install had ever written. Reachable from all five money paths, and generatePeriod calls it once per student — a 200-child madrasa three years in was reading roughly three million rows per nightly auto-invoice run, inside one transaction, on a Raspberry Pi. Fixed with an indexed predicate selecting exactly the rows the JS filter kept.

findings.title: Changing a password did not invalidate the user's other sessions
findings.summary: resetConfirm has always ended every session for the account; changePassword did not. It is the same gesture reached from inside the app and the only revocation a user can perform, since there is no session list and no sign-out-everywhere button. A parent who signed in on a borrowed phone and later changed their password precisely because they were worried left that cookie working for the rest of its 12-hour TTL. Now scoped to that user and sparing the caller's own token. Tier 2: behaviour-visible.

findings.title: Release workflow's GitHub Actions pinned to mutable tags with packages: write
findings.summary: All five actions in the image-publishing job referenced mutable major tags while the job held packages: write and a GHCR-scoped GITHUB_TOKEN. This workflow is the only thing that publishes the artifact masajid install, so a repointed tag does not leak data — it ships a backdoored container under a released version number. cla.yml already pinned its action to a SHA, so the standard was established. Pinned to the SHAs the tags resolved to, so behaviour is unchanged.

findings.title: No CI ran tests, lint, or typecheck; images published unverified
findings.summary: The repo had two workflows, neither of which ran a test. Every push to main published a Docker image to GHCR with nothing having verified that the code compiled or that the 499 tests passed. CLAUDE.md §19 and §9 both claim CI enforces version and alert-id consistency; neither could fire. §9 records the cost: payment-short was raisable in code but undeclared in the manifest for all of 0.43.0, so every such alert was dropped fail-soft, and the guard test written afterwards guarded nothing. Added a lint + test + build workflow on push and PR.

findings.title: Container runs as root
findings.summary: The runtime stage never drops privileges, so a code-execution bug gets uid 0 in-container and unrestricted write to /data, which holds minors' PII and the entire payment ledger. Partially mitigated by cap_drop: ALL and no-new-privileges in compose. Deferred: compose uses a named volume whose ownership Docker seeds from the image only on first creation, so adding USER node would leave every already-deployed masjid unable to open students.db — a boot failure for everyone on update. The correct fix chowns /data then drops privileges via gosu, which could not be verified against a real root-owned volume in this run.

findings.title: @fastify/static 8.3.0 carries 4 HIGH advisories, unreachable in this configuration
findings.summary: Four HIGH advisories: path traversal in directory listing, and three route-guard bypass classes. Rated Low because none is reachable here — the plugin is registered with index: false, no list: true, and no preHandler guard, serving only the built web bundle. There is no guard to bypass and nothing under root that is not already public; the sensitive routes gate themselves separately. Deferred because the fix is a two-major jump (8.3.0 to 10.1.2) to the layer serving every page, and OMS-018 means that layer has no HTTP-level test coverage.

findings.title: drizzle-orm 0.38.3 identifier-escaping SQL injection, unreachable
findings.summary: GHSA-gpj5-g38j-94v9 (HIGH) requires user-controlled input in a SQL identifier position. All 11 raw sql template usages were enumerated: every one interpolates a compile-time schema column reference or a bound parameter, and the only dynamic column selection filters against a hard-coded YEAR_VIEW_COLUMNS allow-list. Deferred because 0.38.3 to 0.45.2 is a major ORM bump across 31 migrations and every money query, to fix a class of bug the code cannot reach.

findings.title: School logo interpolated into an HTML attribute without escaping
findings.summary: The only dynamic value in the server-rendered statement that skipped esc(), while the file's own header promised every dynamic value is escaped. Not exploitable: the value is regex-validated on write and re-validated on read against an anchored data-URI pattern whose alphabet contains no quote or angle bracket, magic bytes must match the declared MIME, SVG is excluded, and only an admin can set it. Fixed because correctness rested entirely on a regex two modules away with no local signal that HTML safety depended on it.

findings.title: Statement HTML served with no CSP or hardening headers
findings.summary: A page assembled by string concatenation containing every child's Student ID and the family's payment history, served same-origin with no Content-Security-Policy, nosniff, referrer policy, or framing protection — while /api/logo in index.ts already set a policy of that shape. Added default-src 'none'; img-src data:; form-action 'none'; frame-ancestors 'none'; base-uri 'none' plus nosniff and no-referrer. 'unsafe-inline' is retained for the one authored style block and Print button, a documented compromise chosen for zero rendering-regression risk; the policy still cuts every external exfiltration channel.

findings.title: Invite acceptance navigates outside the app under the tunnel prefix
findings.summary: window.location.assign('/') was the only navigation in the web app that skipped withBase() and the only location.assign in the codebase. An invite link is opened over the OS tunnel by definition, where the app is served under a prefix like /students, so a parent who had just successfully created their account was redirected to the OS dashboard root — and the session cookie's Path is scoped to that same prefix, so they landed on a page it is not even sent to. Reads as a failed signup, on the primary parent onboarding path.

findings.title: record-payment accepts a currency field and silently ignores it
findings.summary: The contract has carried currency since v1 and this app parsed it, length-validated it, then dropped it. Amounts are integer cents rendered in the school's own currency, so a consumer sending 'eur' against a usd install had EUR 150.00 recorded as $150.00. Requires a consumer bug to trigger, but is silent. Fixed to the safe half only: the mismatch is logged and the money is still recorded, because changing the response would alter a wire contract four repos share and because Stripe has already captured the card — a 422 would strand a real charge. Cross-repo resolution documented in ACTION_REQUIRED.md.

findings.title: Login throttled per-IP only, not per-account
findings.summary: CLAUDE.md §14 requires internet-facing limits per-IP and per-account; only per-IP exists (8 failures / 15 min), so a distributed attacker can grind one known username unthrottled. Deferred as genuinely ambiguous rather than merely consequential: a per-account lockout is a DoS primitive against a named user, and since admin login is LAN-only it would lock out the one person able to fix it. Practical risk is low given argon2id at 19 MiB with a 12-character minimum. Four options offered; per-account alerting without lockout recommended.

findings.title: Base image node:22-slim not digest-pinned
findings.summary: Both build stages use a mutable tag, so two builds of the same commit can produce different images. Deferred and bundled with OMS-007: a multi-arch pin must reference the manifest-list digest or the arm64 build breaks, and this run cannot validate a buildx multi-arch build because CI only runs on pushes to main, which the pre-flight veto forbids. Pinning the wrong digest would break the release pipeline for a reproducibility gain.

findings.title: All dates rendered in UTC with no timezone configuration
findings.summary: No TZ is set in the Dockerfile, compose, or manifest, so the container runs UTC and toISOString().slice(0,10) renders UTC dates. Internally consistent, so no money bug — but for a masjid west of UTC a payment recorded in the evening displays as the next day, on the statement handed to the parent and in the CSV the treasurer reconciles. periodOf() additionally uses local time while everything else uses UTC: harmless at UTC, latent if TZ is ever set. Deferred because a correct fix must apply one timezone to rendering, todayIso(), and period derivation, changing which month a bill lands in.

findings.title: auth.session reports install state over the tunnel
findings.summary: Initially rated Low and fixed by gating setupRequired to LAN origin; the fix was then REVERTED. App.tsx:126 reads the flag together with the origin to render SetupOnLanNotice, a purpose-built component with dedicated i18n copy explaining that the first admin cannot be created over the internet. Gating it would have shown a fresh install's tunnel visitor a generic login form with no accounts and no explanation. The disclosed bit is unactionable because setup refuses every non-LAN origin. Downgraded to Info and accepted by design; a comment now records the decision.

findings.title: Documentation describes removed subsystems as present
findings.summary: CLAUDE.md is declared the single source of truth but describes a Stripe webhook route, stripe_events dedupe table, SMTP settings, a public /apply admissions form, and a 30-row teacher/gradebook/report-card permission matrix — none of which exist after the v0.35.0 descope and the move to platform email. docs/PAYMENTS.md and docker-compose.yml comments carry the same drift, and cla.yml asserted main was branch-protected when the API returns 404 Branch not protected. Fixed the comments in files already being touched; rewriting the specification is owner work.

findings.title: No HTTP-layer tests for the boot path
findings.summary: freshApp() returns tRPC callers with fake contexts and never constructs a Fastify instance, so @fastify/static serving, the SPA notFoundHandler, rewriteUrl base-path stripping, the JSON parser's empty-body path, /api/logo, and /api/public/appearance have no HTTP-level coverage. This is the direct reason OMS-002 and OMS-009 were deferred. Partially addressed: statementRoute.test.ts is the first such coverage, driving the statement route's self-gating access wall through a real Fastify instance.

findings.title: Documented full RTL / Arabic support is plumbing only
findings.summary: CLAUDE.md §4 promises full RTL and §15 an Arabic-capable bundled Naskh face. Actual state: one locale file (en.json), lng hard-coded to 'en', language force-reset at boot, no dir attribute anywhere, and only Inter and Space Grotesk bundled. Not a defect — all strings do route through t(), and the forced reset is a correct guard against a stale ar/ur preference setting dir=rtl on an English UI. The finding is that the documentation claims shipped capability where only groundwork exists.

findings.title: externalRef accepts an unbounded object shape
findings.summary: z.record(z.unknown()) with no key count, depth, or size limit, persisted as JSON on the immutable payments row and bounded only by Fastify's 1 MiB bodyLimit. A buggy consumer holding a valid app secret could store ~1 MiB per payment, bloating the SQLite file and the 30-minute snapshots on a Pi. Low practical concern since callers are secret-gated sibling apps, but the contract only ever needs four known keys. Not fixed: narrowing an accepted request shape is contract-adjacent and belongs with the OMS-015 cross-repo item.

findings.title: Vulnerable transitive dependencies at patch-fixable versions
findings.summary: Five transitive packages had non-breaking fixes available: postcss (moderate, sourceMappingURL arbitrary .map read), find-my-way (high, HTTP/2 DoS — Fastify's router), fast-uri at two versions (high, host confusion via backslash authority), and brace-expansion (high, unbounded expansion OOM). Applied via npm audit fix after confirming by dry-run that it changed five packages and added, removed, and majored nothing. find-my-way is the only one touching runtime behaviour and is covered by the fabric and statement-route tests, which drive real Fastify routing.
